solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take exercise, a drug

parts.note: to do drugs is to take them, so take gives DO
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An instruction to work out, oddly paired with an offer of something illicit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is a slang name for cannabis or any narcotic substance.

clue.text: Force out idle dogs with a kick

indicators.note: a kick sends things flying into disorder, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lazy dogs are booted out of their resting place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a kick' rearranges the letters of IDLE DOGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to shift or push it from its position.

clue.text: Organise time in factory

parts.note: to plan something is to organise it

explanation.surface: A manager urges scheduling the working hours on the shop floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works or manufacturing site.

clue.text: Introduction before gentle walk

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
an amble is a leisurely stroll

explanation.surface: A short opening remark ahead of a leisurely stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A preamble is the opening statement or preface to a speech or document.

clue.text: Thinks tragedy out of order — prospect of a fine day?

indicators.note: letters out of order are jumbled, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a tragedy has gone wrong, then hopes for good weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' rearranges THINKS TRAGEDY. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'red sky at night, shepherd's delight' says a red sunset promises good weather tomorrow.

clue.text: Like gardens to be asymmetrical

parts.note: as means like, in the sense 'as a child'
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: A gardener's taste for lopsided flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the Royal Botanic Gardens in southwest London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is crooked or out of line, hence lopsided.

clue.text: Possible republican slogan in the finance industry

definitions.meaning: split as ..., a call an anti-monarchist might make
the business of banks and finance

explanation.surface: A political catchphrase turning up among bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is a demand to abolish the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Banking names the sector of money lending, deposits and investment.

clue.text: London statue painful to knock over

indicators.note: knocking something over in a down clue turns it upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: A famous statue that would hurt if toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock over' reverses SORE. EROS is the popular name for the statue at Piccadilly Circus, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure atop the Shaftesbury Memorial Fountain in Piccadilly Circus is known as Eros.

clue.text: Advised in fighting retreat having to be reversed

parts.note: war is fighting

indicators.note: reversed says the word for retreat is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Military counsel to turn round during a fighting withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be reversed' turns DEN into NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To warn someone is to caution or counsel them about something.

clue.text: Heading for the main prize after serious effort initially

indicators.note: after puts the prize word behind the initials that precede it
initially means the opening letters of the words serious and effort are taken

parts.note: an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A prize is given after a serious, determined effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means moving towards the sea, the main in old poetic usage.

clue.text: Japanese fighting finish in knockout

indicators.note: in places the word for finish inside the abbreviation for knockout

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
end means finish

explanation.surface: A Japanese bout concluded by knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: After work can choose to take part

indicators.note: after places the container word behind the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Once the day's work is done, someone may decide to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt in is to elect to be involved in a scheme or activity.

clue.text: Our country rejected, hold on for another

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the abbreviation for our country is turned round

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is the home country of The Times
to wait is to pause or stay put for a while

explanation.surface: Someone spurns their homeland and waits to move to a different nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses UK into KU. 'another' means another country, picking up 'country' from earlier in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a Gulf state, a nation other than Britain.

clue.text: Safe signal fully understood

definitions.meaning: a signal that danger has passed

explanation.surface: A signal that danger has passed, plainly understood.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase sounds after an air raid, and also confirms that explanations are grasped.

clue.text: In helpful spirit, one financing our competitor?

parts.note: The Guardian is a rival newspaper to The Times, which publishes this puzzle
an angel is a backer who finances a theatre production

explanation.surface: A benign backer funds a rival newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our' is The Times speaking; THE GUARDIAN is a rival British daily. An angel is a theatrical investor.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a protective spirit thought to watch over a person.

clue.text: Physical structure of a defensive alliance: goodness!

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance
my! is an exclamation of surprise like goodness!

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how a military pact is organised.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the bodily structure of an organism.

clue.text: Supply a fine car

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Providing someone with a good motor.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to provide or yield, as in 'afford an opportunity'.

clue.text: Doctor was not bad

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are rearranged into a spoilt order

explanation.surface: A physician who proved competent after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges WAS NOT. Dr Watson is Sherlock Holmes's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr John Watson is Sherlock Holmes's medical friend and chronicler.

clue.text: Authority is silent?

definitions.meaning: the authority or permission to do something
read as ..., someone says nothing at all (O being zero)

explanation.surface: Power that keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as 'says O': saying zero is saying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: On someone's say-so means on their authority or permission.

clue.text: Country clipped its old coin

indicators.note: clipped means the tail is cut off the country's name

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A nation trimmed the currency it used to have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' removes the last letter of FRANCE. 'its' refers back to the country, so the definition is France's former currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the French currency until the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Native American leaving hospital fast

indicators.note: leaving says the hospital letter departs from the tribal name

parts.note: an Apache is a member of a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American discharged from hospital quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means swiftly, at speed.

clue.text: Little pressure to mourn

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A gentle push to grieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep is to cry, as one does when grieving.

clue.text: Finally coppice thin wood

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word coppice

parts.note: bony means thin, skinny

explanation.surface: A managed woodland ends with skinny trees.
explanation.walkthrough: A coppice is a woodland of trees cut back regularly to make them regrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a dense black timber from tropical trees.

clue.text: Clothes start to look old rubbish

parts.note: garb is clothing
to age is to begin looking old

explanation.surface: Clothing that begins to look worn is fit for the bin.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is refuse or trash, also nonsense.

clue.text: In this port regularly sail over entrance

indicators.note: over places the sailing word before the entrance word

parts.note: ships ply a route when they travel it regularly
a mouth is an entrance, as of a cave or harbour

explanation.surface: Boats sail in and out of this harbour mouth on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal on 'sail', but it belongs to the synonym: ply means sail regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a naval port city in Devon, southwest England.

clue.text: A little grape, a ripe fruit

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small taste of a grape that has ripened.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear is a sweet orchard fruit of the rose family.
